add.term: display (access levels of the observability ladder)
add.quote: A display is the text made available to the monitor (Figure 1c). In the main prompt-visible setting, the three public access levels are | | $\mathcal{O}^{q}_{1}(i,m)=q_{i}\oplus R_{i,m},\quad\mathcal{O}^{q}_{2}(i,m)=q_{i}\oplus R_{i,m}\oplus S_{i,m},$ | | | $\mathcal{O}^{q}_{3}(i,m)=q_{i}\oplus R_{i,m}\oplus S_{i,m}\oplus C_{i,m}.$ | The final, non-public level adds provider-side replay features: | | $\mathcal{O}^{q}_{4}(i,m)=q_{i}\oplus R_{i,m}\oplus S_{i,m}\oplus C_{i,m}\oplus Z_{i,m}.$ |
add.gloss: A display is what the monitor sees: prompt-visible levels q+R, +self-summary S, +trace C, then non-public replay features Z; prompt-withheld variants drop q.

add.quote: For each output-only display $P$ , public monitors may compute features of the visible text $P$ but may not use the task prompt, target-model hidden states, logits, or token probabilities. Prompt-conditioned control displays relax only the task-prompt exclusion.
add.gloss: Public monitors read only the displayed text: no task prompt (except prompt-conditioned controls), hidden states, logits or token probabilities.

add.quote: An $\ell_{2}$ -regularized logistic probe maps the resulting vector to a correctness score (Table A8). AUROC is the probability that the monitor assigns a higher score to a randomly chosen correct run than to a randomly chosen incorrect run. A value of $0.5$ is chance.
add.gloss: Monitor score = probe's predicted correctness from display features; AUROC = probability a correct run outranks an incorrect one (0.5 = chance).

add.quote: For the main prompt-visible ladder, we report | | $q\Delta_{S}=\mathrm{AUROC}(q+R+S)-\mathrm{AUROC}(q+R),$ | | | $q\Delta_{C}=\mathrm{AUROC}(q+R+S+C)-\mathrm{AUROC}(q+R+S),$ | | | $q\Delta_{Z}=\mathrm{AUROC}(q+R+S+C+Z)-\mathrm{AUROC}(q+R+S+C),$ | with $q\Delta_{\mathrm{public}}=\mathrm{AUROC}(q+R+S+C)-\mathrm{AUROC}(q+R)$ and $q\Delta_{\mathrm{full}}=\mathrm{AUROC}(q+R+S+C+Z)-\mathrm{AUROC}(q+R)$ .
add.gloss: What each added component buys the monitor: paired AUROC difference when adding S, C or Z to the previous level; prompt-withheld analogs Δ_S, Δ_C, Δ_Z omit q.

add.quote: We define the normalized excess-AUROC ratio as $r_{\mathrm{AUROC}}=(\mathrm{AUROC}(S)-0.5)/(\mathrm{AUROC}(C)-0.5)$ . Using the unrounded setting means, $r_{\mathrm{AUROC}}=0.874$ (95% descriptive paired setting-bootstrap interval $[0.855,0.896]$ over the 15 observed settings; Table A14). This normalized performance comparison is not an information-retention measure because AUROC is nonlinear and non-additive.
add.gloss: Summary monitor's AUROC above chance relative to the trace monitor's; a normalized performance comparison, explicitly not a measure of information the summary retains.

add.quote: The within-item AUROC is the pairwise concordance between correct and incorrect runs of the same item, with ties counted as one half, computed over discordant items.
add.gloss: Run-level monitoring: share of correct/incorrect run pairs of the same question in which the monitor scores the correct run higher, holding item-level cues fixed.

add.quote: We score the seven remaining displays with the same versioned instruction, mmlu_pro_display_correctness_probability_v1, which requests one bare probability that the displayed run is correct. Requests use medium reasoning effort and no sampling-parameter override, and the judge receives neither the gold answer, reference answer, nor correctness label.

add.quote: Correctness is the monitored property because the labels are defined externally to the monitor and held fixed across the displays being compared.
add.gloss: A monitored property needs labels defined outside the monitor and fixed across displays; hence correctness, and faithfulness or misbehavior would need such labels too.
